title: Finite separable extensions descend to a dense valued subfield
statement: Let $D\subseteq F\subseteq H$ be fields [def-weil-field] with compatible nontrivial nonarchimedean real absolute values. Thus $|a|=0$ exactly when $a=0$, $|ab|=|a||b|$, $|a+b|\leq\max(|a|,|b|)$, and some nonzero element of $D$ has absolute value different from $1$. Assume that $F$ and $H$ are complete for $d(a,b)=|a-b|$, that $D$ is dense in $F$ (every ball of positive radius in $F$ meets $D$), and that $H/F$ is finite separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Here finite means finite-dimensional as a vector space over the smaller field. Then there is a subfield $l\subseteq H$ containing $D$ such that $l/D$ is finite separable, $l$ is dense in $H$, and the subfield of $H$ generated by $F$ and $l$ is $H$.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.4, proof, printed p. 49: descent of a finite separable extension of a completed field by Krasner approximation; stated here for an arbitrary dense valued subfield.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-primitive-element], choose $a\in H$ with $H=F(a)$. Let $f\in F[T]$ be its monic minimal polynomial, of degree $n\ge1$, as in [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. It is separable since $H/F$ is separable. By [def-pc-separable-polynomial] there are $U,V\in F[T]$ with $Uf+Vf'=1$; evaluating at $a$ gives $V(a)f'(a)=1$, so $f'(a)\ne0$.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.4, proof, printed p. 49; explicit expansion of its Krasner descent sentence (primary text https://arxiv.org/html/0707.3953v3#S6.SS3).

proof.text: Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $H$ using [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Give it the extending nonarchimedean spectral norm from [lem-trf-spectral-norm-algebraic-extension], with base $H$: the given absolute value on $H$, rather than a newly chosen value on $H/F$, is thereby preserved. Since every element of $H$ is algebraic over $F$ and every element of $\Omega$ is algebraic over $H$, [lem-sfb-algebraic-element-tower] makes $\Omega/F$ algebraic. The image of $f$ in $\Omega[T]$ is nonzero and factors into $n$ linear factors by [lem-weil-alg-closed-linear-factorization]. Its roots different from $a$ consequently form a finite set $S$. If $S$ is empty put $r=1$; otherwise put $r=\frac12\min_{c\in S}|a-c|$. Thus $r>0$ and $r<|a-c|$ for every other root $c$.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.4, proof, printed p. 49; explicit expansion of its Krasner descent sentence (primary text https://arxiv.org/html/0707.3953v3#S6.SS3).

proof.text: The valuation ring of $H$ is henselian by the explicit henselian-completion clause of [lem-trf-separable-valued-completion-factors], specialized to the identity finite separable extension $H/H$. Indeed $H$ is its own metric completion: the inverse to constant sequences sends a Cauchy sequence to its limit, exists by completeness, is independent of the representative because equivalent sequences have difference tending to zero, and preserves sums, products and absolute values by taking limits. Hence that clause applies to the given ring $\{h\in H:|h|\le1\}$.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.4, proof, printed p. 49; explicit expansion of its Krasner descent sentence (primary text https://arxiv.org/html/0707.3953v3#S6.SS3).

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-henselian-simple-root-stability] over $H$ to $f$, its simple root $a$, and the ball $|b-a|<r$. Its valuation can be written additively as $v(h)=-\log|h|$ for $h\ne0$, with $v(0)=\infty$; its balls are exactly the absolute-value balls and nontriviality is inherited from $D$. The result gives an open coefficient neighbourhood $V\subset H^n$ of $(f_0,\ldots,f_{n-1})$. A finite product of sufficiently small balls lies in $V$; take $\epsilon>0$ smaller than all their radii. By [lem-sfb-monic-dense-approximation], density of $D$ in $F$ gives a monic $g\in D[T]$ of degree $n$ with $|g_i-f_i|<\epsilon$ for all $i$. The coefficient vector, viewed in $H^n$, lies in $V$, since the values on $F$ and $H$ agree. Thus $g$ has a root $b\in H$ with $|a-b|<r$ and $g'(b)\ne0$.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.4, proof, printed p. 49; explicit expansion of its Krasner descent sentence (primary text https://arxiv.org/html/0707.3953v3#S6.SS3).

proof.text: For every root $c\ne a$ of $f$ in $\Omega$, Step 2 and Step 4 give $|a-b|<r<|a-c|$. Apply [lem-sfb-complete-normed-krasner] with base $F$ and algebraic extension $\Omega/F$. Its base is complete, nontrivially normed and nonarchimedean by hypothesis; the norm extends that of $F$ through $H$; $f$ is the separable minimal polynomial of $a$ and splits in $\Omega$. It gives $a\in F(b)$. Since $b\in H=F(a)$, both inclusions hold and $F(b)=H$. The case $S=\varnothing$ satisfies the Krasner inequality vacuously.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.4, proof, printed p. 49; explicit expansion of its Krasner descent sentence (primary text https://arxiv.org/html/0707.3953v3#S6.SS3).

proof.text: Set $l=D(b)\subseteq H$. The monic polynomial $g$ is nonzero and annihilates $b$, so $b$ is algebraic over $D$. Let $m\in D[T]$ be its minimal polynomial [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. By the kernel-generator description there, $g=mq$ for some $q\in D[T]$. Differentiating this finite polynomial identity and evaluating at $b$ gives $0\ne g'(b)=m'(b)q(b)$, hence $m'\ne0$. The irreducible polynomial $m$ is separable by [lem-trf-irreducible-separable-derivative], so [lem-trf-simple-separable-field-extension] gives that $l/D$ is separable algebraic. It is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-simple-algebraic-extension-power-basis]. The subfield generated by $F$ and $l=D(b)$ is $F(b)=H$.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.4, proof, printed p. 49; explicit expansion of its Krasner descent sentence (primary text https://arxiv.org/html/0707.3953v3#S6.SS3).

proof.text: To verify density, apply [lem-weil-pbc-simple-algebraic-extension-power-basis] over $F$ to $b$: it is algebraic over $F$ because the image of $g$ is nonzero and vanishes at $b$. As $H=F(b)$, if $d=[H:F]\ge1$, each $z\in H$ has the form $z=\sum_{i<d}c_i b^i$ with $c_i\in F$. Given $\eta>0$, put $M=\max(1,|b|^{d-1})\ge1$. Choose $e_i\in D$ with $|c_i-e_i|<\eta/M$ using density, and put $w=\sum_{i<d}e_i b^i\in l$. Since $|b|^i\le M$ for $0\le i<d$, the ultrametric inequality gives $|z-w|\le\max_{i<d}|c_i-e_i|\,|b|^i<\eta$. Every positive-radius ball in $H$ meets $l$, completing the assertion.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.4, proof, printed p. 49; explicit expansion of its Krasner descent sentence (primary text https://arxiv.org/html/0707.3953v3#S6.SS3).

tool_uses.why: Generic local continuity of a simple polynomial root, applied only over the complete valued field H. No same-unit node gives simple-root persistence under coefficient perturbation; this replaces no step of the unit route.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q121-aed3d5ffb (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Shape: one commit (item JSON plus report), no new nodes. The statement is byte-identical to live, which is unsplit with no proof, so it is unchanged and not weakened. Small cases checked: ℚ⊂ℚ_p⊂ℚ_p(√p); 𝔽_p(t)⊂𝔽_p((t)) with an Artin–Schreier H; H=F. The Temkin PDF is absent locally, so I did not re-read Cor. 6.3.4; the item's source field is inherited. Steps, against each cited statement read in full. Step 1: primitive element, then the minimal polynomial is separable, then the Bezout identity gives f'(a)≠0. Step 2: the algebraic closure of H has the spectral norm extending |·|_H (H complete and nontrivial); the tower lemma makes Ω/F algebraic; linear factorization gives the finite root set S and 0<r<|a−c|. Step 3: henselianity is the explicit statement clause of lem-trf-separable-valued-completion-factors with F=E=H, using Ĥ≅H. Step 4: lem-per-henselian-simple-root-stability (henselian, f monic, simple root; v=−log|·| gives the same topology) with lem-sfb-monic-dense-approximation (D dense in F, |·|_H restricts to |·|_F) gives b∈H with |a−b|<r and g'(b)≠0. Step 5: complete-normed Krasner over F in Ω (the norm extends |·|_F, f separable and split) gives a∈F(b), so F(b)=H. Step 6: g=mq and g'(b)=m'(b)q(b)≠0, so m'≠0; then the irreducible-derivative, simple-separable and power-basis nodes make D(b)/D finite separable, and the compositum is F(b)=H. Step 7: the power basis of H over F plus the ultrametric bound with M=max(1,|b|^{d−1}) gives density, including d=1 and b=0. Duplicate search (rg -L dense subfield/krasner): the dense-subfield root-approximation, DVR completion-extension, henselian Krasner-neighbourhood and dense-henselian étale nodes differ from the item; there is no duplicate. A DFS from all 16 cited nodes does not reach the item. The single declared tool use, lem-per-henselian-simple-root-stability, is a generic valued-field lemma with no node in sk-i-curve-zero giving it, and is accepted. No SGA. No fixes.
